definitions.explanation: Describing something done poorly or lacking skill. A formal, somewhat literary term used to criticize the quality of work, performance, or technique.

examples.japanese: {拙劣|せつれつ}な{演技|えんぎ}だった。
{拙劣|せつれつ}な{模倣|もほう}にすぎない。
examples.english: It's nothing more than a crude imitation.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}の{拙劣|せつれつ}な{対応|たいおう}が{被害|ひがい}を{拡大|かくだい}させた。
examples.english: The government's poor handling of the situation worsened the damage.

notes: Composed of {拙|せつ} (clumsy, unskillful) + {劣|れつ} (inferior). A formal/written term expressing strong criticism of quality or skill. The opposite is {巧妙|こうみょう} (skillful, clever). Common collocations: {拙劣|せつれつ}な{手口|てぐち} (clumsy tactics), {拙劣|せつれつ}な{技術|ぎじゅつ} (poor technique), {拙劣|せつれつ}な{対応|たいおう} (poor handling). More formal and harsher than {下手|へた} (unskillful, poor at). Related words: {稚拙|ちせつ} (immature, childish — implies lack of sophistication), {粗雑|そざつ} (rough, sloppy).
